_RESOLVED.still_not_wired: The TabFM *district forecast layer* (services/ml/app/forecast/tabfm_forecast.py) has NO SageMaker dispatch - it calls risk/models_iface.get_foundation_model() in process, so it runs on local CPU, not this endpoint. Real GPU TabFM is reachable only via the predict runtime (station_workload_band). Giving the forecast layer a SageMaker path is new feature work, not a fix.
defects_fixed_to_get_here: services/gpu-worker/_tabfm_loader.py held BOTH a ~6.3GB fp32 module AND a full ~6.3GB state dict during load_state_dict, peaking ~13GB and getting SIGKILLed on the 16GB host. Replaced with _stream_load_weights(): per-tensor copy straight from safetensors into pre-allocated params, so peak host RAM is just the module.

An interim fp16 attempt loaded fine (3.3GB VRAM) but produced all-NaN probabilities - this model's activations exceed the fp16 range. Params are now fp32 (6.6GB VRAM, fits the T4) and TabFMClassifier(use_amp=True) still autocasts matmuls to fp16 for tensor-core speed.
backends.run_tabfm/run_timesfm returned NaN results as state=COMPLETED, violating fail-closed. Added an output finiteness guard that raises BackendUnavailable.

sagemaker_ops.py _poll only watched the output key, so a fast container failure burned the entire timeout (cost a 25-minute false 'timeout'). It now also polls <failure-prefix>/<inference-id>-error.out.

sagemaker_ops.py had no update path - 'deploy' is create-only and silently keeps the old image via _safe [exists]. Added a 'redeploy' subcommand that versions model+endpoint-config by image digest and calls update_endpoint.
codebuild_image.py's CodeBuild role lacked kms:Decrypt, so it could not read the source zip once the bucket defaulted to the model-plane CMK.
iam/sagemaker-exec-policy.json hardcoded the dead account 860510875713 in every ARN.

backends._timesfm_infer_core rebuilt TimesFM_2p5_200M_torch on EVERY request and never freed it, so 37 district forecasts accumulated ~14.13 GiB of PyTorch allocations beside the pinned TabFM model until 'CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB'. Added an lru_cache'd _load_timesfm(); this also cut per-request latency from ~5.2s of model loading to ~0.2s of inference.

SageMakerTimesFMForecaster keyed idempotency on f'timesfm:{last_period}:{horizon}:{len(series)}' with NO district or series content, so all 37 districts collided on one key and the adapter replayed district 1's forecast into all 37 rows. Now keyed on a sha256 of (last_period, horizon, series). This could never have shown up before today because the SageMaker path was unreachable while GPU quota was 0.

sagemaker_ops._register_autoscaling created ONLY a target-tracking policy on ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance. With min_capacity=0 that metric is undefined at 0 instances, so the endpoint accepted invocations, parked them in the backlog and NEVER provisioned a GPU - requests hung until the caller timed out. Added the required StepScaling policy driven by a HasBacklogWithoutCapacity CloudWatch alarm, plus an 'autoscale' subcommand to repair a live endpoint. Verified: alarm -> ALARM, desired 0->1, instance up in ~4 min.

SageMakerTimesFMForecaster hardcoded poll_timeout_s=300, shorter than a scale-from-zero cold start, producing a spurious 'dispatch did not complete: state=RUNNING'. Now DRISHTI_TIMESFM_POLL_TIMEOUT_S, default 1200.

The dispatch RuntimeError discarded error_detail, so a CUDA OOM and a licence/digest rejection both read as 'error=INFERENCE_ERROR' and the cause had to be dug out of the S3 result object by hand. It now includes detail.
_RESOLVED.known_issue_not_fixed: The adapter's IdempotencyStore persists FAILED results under the idempotency key, so a transient infrastructure failure (e.g. the CUDA OOM) is replayed forever for that input and the work can never be retried. Clearing async-io/idem/ + async-io/jobs/ is the current workaround. Idempotency should memoize successful work only, or cache failures with a short TTL.
